name: Ahmad Assi
positioning: I design buildings that hold up under a prairie winter and still feel generous in it. Eleven years across housing, civic and cultural work, most of it spent on the drawings that get built.
longBio: I came to architecture through building. Three summers framing houses outside Edmonton taught me that a detail either works at minus thirty or it does not, and that most of what separates a good building from a merely handsome one is decided long after the concept is signed off.

Since then I have worked mostly in the middle of projects, where design intent meets a real budget. I run drawing sets, resolve envelopes, and sit in the meetings where a decision is either defended or quietly lost. I am equally comfortable presenting to a council committee and standing on a site in a hard hat explaining why a joint matters.
My own interest is in cold climate public space: how a building can make winter usable rather than merely survivable. Most of my competition work circles that question.

contributions: Lead architect on two civic projects through construction, the larger at 4,200 square metres.
Rebuilt the office envelope detail library after a moisture failure on an earlier project, now standard on every job.
Run the drawing set: coordination, consultant integration, and the specification.
Delivered eleven mid rise residential permit sets, six of which are built.
Led the firm's move from drafted details to a coordinated model, which cut consultant clashes noticeably.
Competition drawings, physical models, and the parts of a set nobody volunteers for.
Site review on a heritage retrofit, twice weekly for fourteen months.
Framing, sheathing and forming on single family houses. The reason I detail the way I do.
